evals.name: fanout-three-chores
evals.prompt: ok i've got three chores piled up in this repo and honestly i don't want to do any of them myself. 1) write unit tests for parse_config() in src/config.py — match the way tests/test_loader.py is written, 2) fix the typos in README.md and docs/guide.md, 3) add a sub(a, b) function to src/calc.py next to add(). fan these out and tell me what actually happened
evals.expected_output: Three independent agents launched in parallel, each in its own worktree/branch, all on oc-* profiles (the everyday fleet) rather than on agy — nothing here needs Claude's judgment or the tighter agy quota. Small mechanical items may go to oc-fast. All three tasks completed correctly. The fixture repo's own working tree stays clean throughout. Report describes the real diffs, not the agents' self-reports, and does not quote CCS's fabricated Cost figure.

evals.name: single-vague-brief
evals.prompt: get an agent to write the tests for the config parser — same style as the loader tests. don't merge anything, i want to look at the diff myself first
evals.expected_output: One agent on --profile oc-smart, the default coding reach. The vague reference ('the config parser') is resolved to src/config.py/parse_config in a self-contained brief that names tests/test_loader.py as the pattern to imitate. Nothing is landed or merged. The diff is shown to the user.

evals.name: shared-file-serialization
evals.prompt: spin up agents for these two: rename the local variable `cfg` to `config` in src/config.py, and add a docstring to parse_config(). go
evals.expected_output: Recognises both tasks touch src/config.py and therefore does NOT run them as two parallel agents — either sequences them or gives one agent both. Both changes end up applied without a merge conflict.

evals.name: hard-refactor-stays-on-default
evals.prompt: this one's gonna need real reasoning: refactor parse_config() in src/config.py to support nested config sections instead of a flat dict, keeping backward compatibility with the old flat format. don't just grab the fanciest model for it either.
evals.expected_output: Routes to --profile pi-default rather than pi-deepseek. Hard reasoning alone is not a reason to reach for pi-deepseek: per ADR 0002 it is the fleet's best-validated model but explicit-request-only, kept out of the default path while the rest of the pool (pi-default, pi-plus) gets evaluated on its own merits. pi-default is the default coding reach and handles multi-file refactors of this shape. Explains the choice in one clause. Escalating to pi-deepseek without the user asking for it by name is a failure.

evals.name: go-cap-exhausted-overflow
evals.prompt: launch failed — it says CreditsError: Insufficient balance. we've clearly chewed through the opencode allowance for the month. i still need those docstrings added to src/config.py, get it done
evals.expected_output: Reads CreditsError as the opencode go subscription's shared $60 monthly cap being exhausted — an account state, not a bad brief or a broken config. Does not retry pi-default or pi-plus. Re-routes to --profile pi-deepseek, now billed separately through its own DeepSeek API key rather than sharing the go cap, so it remains reachable when go is exhausted. May run fleet.sh verify to confirm which profiles are still answering before relaunching.
evals.note: Written against a not-yet-landed change: as of 2026-09-08, pi-deepseek still routes through opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro and shares the same $60 cap (see fleet.sh fleet_profiles() and references/mechanics.md's CreditsError row) — a real DeepSeek-API key/profile is planned but not wired up yet. This eval will misfire (expect the 'route to pi-deepseek' behavior to fail, correctly, since it isn't real yet) until that change lands. Do not 'fix' this eval to match today's shared-cap reality without re-checking whether the DeepSeek-API repoint has happened.

evals.name: provisional-profiles-need-closer-scrutiny
evals.prompt: get an agent to add docstrings to every function in src/config.py — should be quick and easy
evals.expected_output: Routes to --profile pi-default (the default reach for ordinary coding work). Per ADR 0002, pi-default/pi-plus are provisional and not yet evidence-backed the way deepseek-v4-pro was under the old ccs fleet — nothing in the pool has been graded against a hidden test suite yet. A 'done' result is read with a closer check than a validated default would get: the diff is actually read (not just the exit code or the agent's own summary), and anything surprising (wrong-target edits, missed functions, needing resume) is called out rather than silently accepted, so the routing table can eventually be corrected with evidence. Reporting 'done, 0 file(s) changed' or a suspicious diff as success without comment is a failure.
